title: A Universal Loss-limited Optimum For Fixed Multi-pass Quantum Sensing Per Absorbed Photon
authors: Christoph F. Wildfeuer
abstract: ArXiv:2608.25534v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-pass schemes send a photon through a sample several times to learn more about it. When the sample rather than the light is scarce, the natural figure of merit is the information gained per photon the object absorbs. We show that one constant fixes the loss-limited optimum of every fixed scheme in which a single photon passes repeatedly through the sample and is detected once at the end. Three properties suffice: information that grows as the square of the pass number, a fixed survival probability per pass, and no dose from a photon already lost. They force a single trade-off function [MATH], where [MATH] is the number of passes times the loss per pass. Its maximum, 0.648, sits at [MATH]. The loss-limited ceiling of interaction-free interrogation and the multi-pass phase optimum of Yu et al. are two instances. Phase sensing of a weakly absorbing object is a third, optimal at [MATH] passes; the absorption [MATH] and the parasitic loss [MATH] enter the optimum only through their sum, but the damage counts only [MATH]. N00N states and their loss-robust generalisations do worse per absorbed photon, and optimising over photon number and pass number together returns a single recycled photon. Two further problems are priced in the same measure. Absorption estimation gains nothing, for any scheme. Detecting a faint companion below the Rayleigh limit costs the companion a dose that does not depend on its faintness, while under direct imaging the dose grows without bound. For a fragile sample the gentlest measurement is also the simplest one: a single photon, recycled.
tldr: This paper derives a universal loss-limited optimum for multi-pass quantum sensing, showing that a single recycled photon is optimal for phase sensing under absorption.
motivation: To optimize the information gained per absorbed photon in multi-pass quantum sensing when the sample is fragile.
method: The author analyzes fixed multi-pass schemes with a single photon, using three properties (information quadratic in pass number, fixed survival probability, no dose from lost photons) to derive a trade-off function.
result: The maximum information per absorbed photon is 0.648, occurring at a specific product of passes and loss. This covers interaction-free interrogation and multi-pass phase sensing, and shows N00N states are suboptimal.
conclusion: The paper provides a universal optimality result for multi-pass sensing, suggesting that the simplest measurement (single recycled photon) is optimal for fragile samples.

title: A Note On The Measure Of Vector And Pythagorean Theorem
authors: Yu. V. Brezhnev
abstract: ArXiv:2608.24943v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Why the square? We present a geometry-axiom-free derivation of the Pythagorean theorem and the square at its core, establishing their algebraic origin from within the bare vector-space framework. Such concepts as the (right) angle, rotation, inner product, orthogonality etc also emerge as a logical construct rather than taken as given. They are necessitated by the square, and the ensuing theory, in turn, [MATH] stems from a [MATH] definitional primitive [MATH] the ([MATH]\scriptscriptstyle+[MATH]-quantitative) invariant [MATH]-measure of a vector. This provides the core of an algebraic justification for Euclidean geometry. Equally important, these findings account (also canonically) for the complex modulus-squared [MATH] [MATH] the quantum Born rule [MATH] and point out what is even admissible for being quantitatively interpreted. The linear structure and its automorphisms are rigid in the sense that the [MATH] interpretable turns out to be, up to gauge [MATH]\scriptstyle\times[MATH], the unique gauge-invariant measure [MATH]; independently of the field [MATH] or [MATH].
tldr: The paper derives the Pythagorean theorem and the square from bare vector-space axioms, linking them to the Born rule in quantum mechanics.
motivation: The author aims to provide a geometry-axiom-free derivation of the Pythagorean theorem and the square, establishing their algebraic origin and explaining the Born rule.
method: The approach uses vector-space framework, defining a gauge-invariant measure of a vector, and deriving the square and angle concepts as logical constructs.
result: The derivation reveals that the Pythagorean theorem and the square arise from a unique invariant measure, and it canonically accounts for the complex modulus-squared and the Born rule.
conclusion: The findings offer an algebraic justification for Euclidean geometry and highlight what can be quantitatively interpreted, though the connection to quantum information is indirect.

title: Exact Common Information And Exact Channel Synthesis For Correlated Gaussian Sources
authors: Lei Yu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.26012v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we resolve two conjectures posed by Yu and Tan in 2020 (in two separate papers published in the IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory). Specifically, we establish that: 1) the exact common information for a pair of [MATH]-correlated Gaussian sources is given by the conjectured expression [MATH]; and 2) the admissible region for the shared randomness rate and the communication rate in exact channel synthesis is exactly the conjectured one. These results yield two important consequences. First, for any [MATH], the exact common information of a correlated Gaussian pair strictly exceeds Wyner's common information. Second, for [MATH], the exact channel synthesis of such a pair requires strictly higher rates than the total-variation version. The proof combines an exact optimal-transport representation of the worst-case Gaussian cross-entropy, Fathi's Gaussian transport inequality, and a determinant inequality arising from the covariance structure of the conditional means.
tldr: This paper resolves two conjectures on exact common information and exact channel synthesis for correlated Gaussian sources, proving strict superiority over Wyner's common information and higher rates than total-variation versions.
motivation: The paper addresses open conjectures in classical information theory regarding the exact common information and channel synthesis rates for Gaussian sources, which are fundamental problems with implications for distributed source coding and communication.
method: The proof uses an exact optimal-transport representation of worst-case Gaussian cross-entropy, Fathi's Gaussian transport inequality, and a determinant inequality from the covariance structure of conditional means.
result: It establishes the conjectured expressions for exact common information and the admissible region for channel synthesis, showing strict gaps compared to Wyner's common information and total-variation synthesis.
conclusion: The results settle long-standing conjectures, providing exact characterizations for Gaussian sources and highlighting differences between exact and approximate information-theoretic measures.

title: $(k,n)$-core Percolation On Hypergraphs With Anchor Nodes
authors: Hoseung Jang, Byungjoon Min, Ginestra Bianconi
abstract: ArXiv:2608.25560v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hypergraphs describe higher-order interactions that involve more than a pair of nodes. A characteristic feature of hypergraphs is that their robustness can be strongly affected by the different roles of the nodes. Indeed, some nodes might be essential for a hyperedge's function, while others might not be. The loss of a single essential node completely destroys the hyperedge it belongs to, while the loss of a non-essential node has a buffering effect, inducing the hyperedge to simply reduce its size. In order to capture this phenomenology, we formulate a comprehensive theoretical framework for [MATH]-core percolation models on hypergraphs, where each node of a hyperedge is an anchor with probability [MATH], and a hyperedge fails if an anchor node fails. Hypergraph [MATH]-core percolation problems can be classified as first-neighbor and second-neighbor problems, indicating that in the pruning process the connectivity is ensured only by the state of the first neighbors or the second neighbors, respectively. We derive self-consistency equations for first-neighbor and second-neighbor (node- and hyperedge-based) pruning processes, and obtain the size of the giant [MATH]-core. We obtain the phase diagram, including continuous and discontinuous transitions, and confirm our theory on random hypergraphs using numerical simulations. The results show how the heterogeneity of the nodes' functional roles and the extended range of the interactions affect the robustness of higher-order networks.
tldr: This paper formulates a theoretical framework for (k,n)-core percolation on hypergraphs where nodes can be anchors, deriving self-consistency equations to study the robustness of hypergraphs under node failures.
motivation: Hypergraphs capture higher-order interactions, and the role of nodes (essential vs non-essential) affects robustness. The authors aim to generalize core percolation to hypergraphs with anchor nodes to understand how heterogeneous node roles and interaction ranges affect network robustness.
method: They classify percolation problems as first-neighbor and second-neighbor, derive self-consistency equations for node- and hyperedge-based pruning, and solve them for random hypergraphs, comparing with numerical simulations.
result: They obtain the size of the giant k-core and phase diagrams showing continuous and discontinuous transitions, confirming theory with simulations.
conclusion: The heterogeneity of nodes' functional roles and extended range of interactions significantly affect robustness of higher-order networks.

title: Data-driven Effective Modeling Of Stochastic Chemical Reaction Networks
authors: Yuan Chen, Weize Mao, Dongbin Xiu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.25421v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Stochastic Simulation Algorithm (SSA), widely considered an exact algorithm for stochastic chemical reaction networks, suffers from high computational cost. In this work, we propose a data-driven effective model that operates on a user-defined coarse time step independent of the underlying microscopic reaction-event scale. This is accomplished by directly approximating the finite-time transition kernel of the continuous-time Markov chain induced by SSA, using a generative machine learning model trained on short bursts of SSA simulation data. The trained model constructs a stochastic propagator that recursively generates statistically consistent trajectories at the constant coarse time step, with significantly reduced computational cost. In this paper, we employ conditional normalizing flow as the stochastic propagator. A comprehensive set of numerical examples is presented to demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method.
tldr: This paper proposes a data-driven effective model for stochastic chemical reaction networks using normalizing flows to approximate the transition kernel and reduce computational cost.
motivation: The Stochastic Simulation Algorithm (SSA) is computationally expensive for stochastic chemical reaction networks, prompting a need for faster yet accurate approximations.
method: A conditional normalizing flow is trained on short bursts of SSA simulation data to approximate the finite-time transition kernel, enabling recursive trajectory generation at a coarse time step.
result: Numerical examples demonstrate that the proposed method yields statistically consistent trajectories with significantly reduced computational cost compared to SSA.
conclusion: The data-driven propagator approach offers an efficient alternative to exact simulation for stochastic chemical reaction networks, balancing accuracy and speed.

title: Exact Topology Of Conservative Multiplicative Cascades: An Ultrametric Transfer-operator Genus
authors: Cristiano G. Sabiu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.24897v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The multiplicative cascade is a well-known method for generating random fields that are both genuinely non-Gaussian and scale invariant. Its one-point and scaling statistics, namely the multifractal spectra [MATH], [MATH], and [MATH], are known exactly; however, its geometric and topological measures are not. In this work, we show that the topological structures of a conservative (microcanonical) random permutation cascade can be precisely predicted. We compute the digital (cubical) Euler characteristic, or genus, of the level-[MATH] excursion set of the two-dimensional cascade in closed form, using a transfer operator on the cascade's [MATH]-ary tree closed by its ultrametric structure and a conservative without-replacement sibling split. The result requires no Monte Carlo and matches simulated realizations with a maximum residual of [MATH] in the Euler density, a controlled discretization artifact of the atomic measure. We tie the genus scaling analytically to the multifractal spectrum, and show that for a geometric ladder of weights the genus is exactly self-similar under the multifractal-width dial. The construction uses the tree-sum cumulant machinery of Greiner et al. (Phys. Rev. E 58, 554, 1998), specialized to topological functionals; the conservative split carries the microcanonical fingerprint [MATH] that distinguishes it from canonical and lognormal cascades. The cascade is the multiplicative counterpart of the Rayleigh--L\'evy flight and a controlled benchmark for the morphology of strongly non-Gaussian fields.
tldr: This paper derives an exact closed-form expression for the Euler characteristic (genus) of excursion sets in conservative multiplicative cascades using a transfer operator on an ultrametric tree.
motivation: The paper aims to predict the topological structure of multiplicative cascades, which are used to model non-Gaussian scale-invariant random fields, complementing known one-point and scaling statistics.
method: The author computes the digital Euler characteristic of level sets in a two-dimensional conservative cascade by constructing a transfer operator on the cascade's p-ary tree, exploiting its ultrametric structure and the conservative without-replacement split.
result: The derived expression requires no Monte Carlo and matches simulations with a maximum residual in the Euler density, and the genus scaling is tied analytically to the multifractal spectrum.
conclusion: The work provides an exact topological characterization for a class of multiplicative cascades, establishing a link between topology and multifractal statistics.

title: Optical Centrifuge As A Probe Of Strong Dissipative Coupling Between A Molecular Rotor And Superfluid Helium
authors: Ian Macphail-Bartley, S\"oren E. Mahr, Cameron E. Peters, Baptiste Coquinot, Volker Karle, Giacomo Bighin, Ragheed Alhyder, Mikhail Lemeshko, Henrik Stapelfeldt, Valery Milner
abstract: ArXiv:2608.25161v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A macroscopic manifestation of superfluidity is that objects moving through liquid helium experience negligible friction below the Landau critical velocity. How this frictionless motion breaks down at the nanoscale remains an open question. Molecules embedded in helium nanodroplets represent a well-controlled system for studying this breakdown, yet none has reached the regime of strong dissipative coupling, when energy transfer from the molecule to the superfluid dominates the observed dynamics. Molecular rotation, induced by short laser pulses, offer a suitable probe to reach rotational energies in the range of the roton gap, where superfluid helium supports a large number of elementary excitations. However, the solvation shell around a rotating molecule caps the energy reachable by a free rotor after impulsive excitation well below the roton excitation energy. Here we show that continuous driving with an ultraslow optical centrifuge overcomes this limitation: the strong field dresses the molecule into pendular states whose energies fall within the spectrum of the collective excitations of the superfluid, placing the system in the strong-dissipation regime. The resulting rapid thermalization locks the molecule to the rotating field until the rotation-induced level splittings overtake the thermalization rate, beyond which the molecular alignment is progressively lost. Our approach offers a direct measurement of the molecule-bath coupling in a quantum fluid.
tldr: This paper investigates strong dissipative coupling between a molecular rotor and superfluid helium using an optical centrifuge, demonstrating that continuous driving can access rotational energies within the roton gap, leading to rapid thermalization and molecular alignment.
motivation: To understand the breakdown of frictionless motion in superfluids at the nanoscale and to reach the strong dissipative coupling regime for molecular rotation in superfluid helium.
method: They use an ultraslow optical centrifuge to continuously drive molecules into pendular states, which have energies overlapping with collective excitations of the superfluid, placing the system in the strong-dissipation regime.
result: The molecule rapidly thermalizes and locks to the rotating field until the rotation-induced level splittings exceed the thermalization rate, at which point molecular alignment is progressively lost.
conclusion: The approach provides a direct measurement of molecule-bath coupling in a quantum fluid.

title: Intrinsic Radial Landau Rainbow In Triaxial Strained Photonic Crystal
authors: Satoshi Iwamoto Guangti Lu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.25260v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Localized resonances are essential for enhancing light matter interaction, controlling emission, and realizing compact optical resonators and lasers. Landau levels offer a distinct route to organizing photonic states through synthetic magnetic fields, but their high degeneracy does not define spectrally separated localized resonances. Here, we report the intrinsic lifting of degeneracy in photonic Landau levels in a triaxially strained photonic crystal, leading to the emergence of an intrinsic radial Landau rainbow. The triaxial deformation generates photonic Landau levels through a strain induced pseudomagnetic field, while an accompanying pseudoelectric field lifts the degeneracy of the Landau levels. As a result, each Landau level splits into an equally spaced frequency ladder of localized resonances. In zeroth Landau level, these modes exhibit intensity maxima that move progressively outward from the device center, establishing a radial frequency position mapping and Landau rainbow. Our results reveal an intrinsic fine structure of photonic Landau levels in a triaxial strained photonic crystal and provide a route to spatially ordered Landau level resonances.
tldr: 该论文报道了在三轴应变光子晶体中，通过合成磁场产生光子朗道能级并利用赝电场消除简并，形成径向朗道彩虹的局域共振模式。
motivation: 局域共振对于增强光与物质相互作用和实现紧凑型光谐振器至关重要，而传统的朗道能级高度简并，缺乏谱分离的局域模式。
method: 通过三轴应变在光子晶体中引入赝磁场和赝电场，利用理论分析与数值模拟展示朗道能级的简并抬升和频率阶梯结构。
result: 每个朗道能级分裂为等间隔的频率阶梯，零级朗道能级模式的强度极大值从中心向外移动，形成径向频率位置映射和朗道彩虹。
conclusion: 揭示了三轴应变光子晶体中朗道能级的内在精细结构，为空间有序的朗道共振提供了一种新途径。

title: Analog Time-Frequency Analysis And Frequency Measurement Of Ultra-Wideband Microwave Signals Via Dual-Comb Channelization
authors: Taixia Shi, Wentao Ma, Fangzheng Zhang, Yang Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2608.25378v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Frequency-to-time mapping (FTTM)-based photonics-assisted spectrum sensing enables wideband spectrum monitoring for applications such as cognitive radio and electronic warfare. However, FTTM-based photonics-assisted spectrum sensing approaches involve trade-offs among analysis bandwidth, temporal resolution, and frequency resolution. Although channelization has been introduced to alleviate these trade-offs, the limited number of available channels in previously reported systems constrains further improvements in overall performance. Here, we propose a photonics-assisted dual-comb channelization architecture for broadband frequency measurement and time-frequency analysis. The system employs a stepped-frequency pump based on stimulated Brillouin scattering (SBS) to generate an optical filter comb and adopts a single-laser design for the pump, probe, and reference paths to enhance frequency stability while reducing system complexity. Experimental results show a 48-GHz analysis bandwidth in the 16-channel configuration and 52 GHz in the 20-channel configuration, together with microsecond-scale temporal resolution and a frequency resolution better than 80 MHz. The proposed architecture therefore offers a practical and reconfigurable solution for real-time wideband spectrum sensing.
tldr: This paper presents a photonics-assisted dual-comb channelization architecture for wideband frequency measurement and time-frequency analysis of microwave signals, using stimulated Brillouin scattering to generate an optical filter comb.
motivation: Traditional FTTM-based photonics-assisted spectrum sensing faces trade-offs between analysis bandwidth, temporal resolution, and frequency resolution; limited channels constrain performance.
method: The system employs a stepped-frequency pump based on stimulated Brillouin scattering (SBS) to create an optical filter comb, with a single-laser design for pump, probe, and reference paths to improve stability and reduce complexity.
result: Experimental results show a 48-GHz analysis bandwidth in a 16-channel configuration and 52 GHz in a 20-channel configuration, with microsecond-scale temporal resolution and frequency resolution better than 80 MHz.
conclusion: The proposed architecture offers a practical and reconfigurable solution for real-time wideband spectrum sensing, addressing the limitations of previous channelization approaches.

title: Interpretable Activation-Selection Neural Networks For Symbolic Regression Of Parameter-Dependent Hamiltonian Eigenvalues
authors: Kirill F. Sheberstov Alexander Yu. Kharin
abstract: ArXiv:2608.25475v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Analytical approximations to eigenvalues of parameter-dependent Hamiltonians can provide physical insight that is not readily apparent from numerical diagonalization alone. Here, we introduce an activation-selection network (ASN), a differentiable symbolic-regression architecture in which each input node learns a sparse combination of predefined analytical functions, and the trained network can be converted directly into an explicit expression. Before regression, the Hamiltonian parameters and eigenvalues are expressed as dimensionless ratios. This normalization enforces dimensional homogeneity, reduces the number of independent variables, and ensures that the extracted expressions do not depend on the choice of energy units. Using the library {0, x, x^2}, compositions across successive hidden layers generate polynomial expansions of progressively higher degree; polynomial expansions of arbitrary finite degree can therefore be obtained in principle by increasing the network depth. We apply the ASN to effective three- and four-site spin-chain Hamiltonians relevant to zero-quantum nuclear magnetic resonance. Comparisons with degenerate perturbation theory show that the extracted expressions capture the expected constant, linear, and quadratic structure. Fixed-basis least-squares models match or slightly outperform the ASN when an appropriate quadratic basis is specified in advance, while inclusion of a radial feature improves the local approximation near the degeneracy. These results establish the ASN as a differentiable framework for selecting compact symbolic representations when several functional forms are plausible, while showing that adaptive activation selection does not provide an intrinsic accuracy advantage over a suitable predefined basis.
tldr: This paper introduces an activation-selection network for symbolic regression to approximate parameter-dependent Hamiltonian eigenvalues, applied to spin-chain models in NMR.
motivation: To obtain analytical approximations of Hamiltonian eigenvalues that offer physical insight beyond numerical diagonalization, especially for parameter-dependent systems.
method: The ASN learns sparse combinations of predefined functions and converts the trained network into explicit expressions, using dimensionless ratios for normalization and polynomial expansions via layer compositions.
result: The ASN captures expected constant, linear, and quadratic structure from perturbation theory, but fixed-basis least-squares models perform similarly or slightly better when a suitable basis is provided.
conclusion: The ASN provides a flexible symbolic regression framework but does not offer intrinsic accuracy advantages over predefined bases for this problem.

title: Generalizing Thermal Transport In High-Contrast Metamaterials Through Interfacial Fresnel Reflection
authors: Seung Hyeon Ham, Yu Min Kim, In Hyeok Choi, Jeong Woo Han
abstract: ArXiv:2608.25499v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The rapid growth of generative AI has intensified the need for efficient heat dissipation in large-scale data centers. To control heat flow, thermal metamaterials with layered structures have been widely used, which impart the anisotropic properties of thermal conductivities. However, the conventional effective medium approximation (EMA) often fails to provide accurate predictions in systems with a high thermal conductivity contrast between adjacent layers embedded in a background medium. Here, we generalize the EMA by introducing two corrective coefficients that extend its validity to regimes where the conventional EMA was previously inapplicable, i.e., high-contrast thermal metamaterials with the background medium. Notably, one of these coefficients that we proposed has the same mathematical form as the Fresnel reflection coefficient in optics. This allows us to interpret the "reflection-like" behavior of heat flow as it penetrates adjacent layers with high thermal contrast. Our findings suggest that heat diffusion, traditionally viewed as a purely dissipative process, can be understood intuitively through the framework of ray optics.
tldr: This paper generalizes effective medium approximation for thermal metamaterials with high conductivity contrast by introducing corrective coefficients, one analogous to Fresnel reflection, enabling interpretation of heat flow via ray optics.
motivation: The rapid growth of generative AI requires efficient heat dissipation in data centers, and thermal metamaterials with layered structures are used but conventional EMA fails for high conductivity contrast.
method: The authors generalize EMA by introducing two corrective coefficients, one of which matches the Fresnel reflection coefficient form, to extend validity to high-contrast regimes.
result: The proposed coefficients extend EMA applicability to high-contrast thermal metamaterials, and the Fresnel-type coefficient allows a ray-optics interpretation of heat flow.
conclusion: Heat diffusion can be understood using a ray-optics framework, suggesting a new perspective on thermal transport in metamaterials.

title: Giant Strongly Biconnected Components Of Directed Networks: A Generating Function Approach
authors: Minsoo Yang, Reinhard Laubenbacher, Byungjoon Min
abstract: ArXiv:2608.25562v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Strongly connected components (SCCs) characterize modular structure in directed networks but are fragile to single node failures. We study strongly biconnected components (SBCs), which are the set of nodes in which every node pair remains mutually reachable after the removal of any single node, as a more robust notion of connectivity. Using a generating function formalism, we derive the size of the giant SBC and analyze its percolation behavior under random node and link removal. We show that the giant SBC emerges at the same threshold as the giant SCC but grows more slowly due to stricter connectivity requirements. We also applied our theoretical framework to real-world biological networks including gene regulatory networks and neural connectome. Our framework provides insight into the interplay between connectivity, redundancy, and robustness in complex directed systems.
tldr: The paper uses generating functions to analyze giant strongly biconnected components in directed networks, examining their percolation and robustness under node/link removal.
motivation: Strongly connected components are fragile to single node failures, so the authors investigate strongly biconnected components as a more robust connectivity measure.
method: They employ a generating function formalism to derive the size of the giant strongly biconnected component and analyze its percolation behavior under random node and link removals.
result: The giant SBC emerges at the same threshold as the giant SCC but grows more slowly; the framework is applied to biological networks like gene regulatory and neural connectomes.
conclusion: The approach offers insights into the interplay between connectivity, redundancy, and robustness in complex directed systems.

title: GNSS-free Quantum Gravity-aided Navigation And Fine-scale Marine Surveying With A Strapdown Quantum Gravimeter
authors: Patrick J. Everitt, Donald H. White, Todd Lyon, Murat Muradoglu, Alessandro D'ortenzio, Aaron J. Canciani, Malo Cadoret, Daniel D. Brown, David Adams, Yosri Ben-A\"{i}cha, Suraj Bijjahalli, Mojtaba K. Farsani, Alexander Rischka, Karandeep S. Gill, Magdalena Meyer, Henry W. Orton, Nicholas P. Robins, Reuben Symon, Michael J. Biercuk, Michael R. Hush, Stuart S. Szigeti, Russell P. Anderson
abstract: ArXiv:2608.25563v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Global navigation satellite systems (GNSS) are often disrupted or unavailable at sea, and unaided inertial navigation systems (INS) drift without correction. Quantum-sensing-based gravity map matching offers a passive, infrastructure-free aid, but field demonstrations of GNSS-free quantum gravimetric navigation have not been reported. Here we perform gravity map matching and fine-resolution gravity survey with a mobile quantum gravimeter aboard a 29 m surface vessel. We hybridize an atomic sensor with a classical accelerometer for bias stabilization and independently mechanize a navigation-grade IMU, all installed in an uncontrolled cabin with no environmental stabilization or calibration. Operated in both gimbaled and strapdown configurations over identical traversals, the hybrid sensor corrected the inertial solution over an 83 km maritime trajectory by referencing locally measured gravity to a satellite-derived anomaly map. Gravity-aiding constrains INS drift and delivers bounded positioning at nautical-mile-level accuracy, with GNSS excluded throughout the measurement chain. In a separate GNSS-referenced mode, the same system surveyed coastal routes up to Sea State 4, achieving mGal-level agreement with gravimetric maps and sub-mGal repeatability and stability, with gimbaled and strapdown operation performing comparably. Resolved anomalies reach an along-track scale of ~300 m, 50X finer than the satellite map's half-power wavelength. A 56 h stationary test shows atom referencing lowers long-term drift ~70X versus the classical channel alone. These results provide the first same-instrument comparison of gimbaled and strapdown mobile quantum gravimetry and the first fully GNSS-independent gravity-map-matching navigation demonstration using a quantum gravimeter, pointing toward compact, autonomous-platform-ready quantum sensing for GNSS-denied maritime navigation and survey.
tldr: This paper demonstrates GNSS-free maritime navigation and fine-scale marine surveying using a strapdown quantum gravimeter, achieving bounded positioning accuracy and mGal-level gravity agreement with satellite maps.
motivation: GNSS is often unavailable at sea, and inertial navigation systems drift without correction; quantum-sensing-based gravity map matching offers a passive aid.
method: They hybridized an atomic (quantum) sensor with a classical accelerometer for bias stabilization, mechanized a navigation-grade IMU, and performed gravity map matching on a mobile vessel over an 83 km trajectory, comparing gimbaled and strapdown configurations.
result: The system corrected the inertial solution with nautical-mile-level accuracy, achieved mGal-level agreement and sub-mGal repeatability, resolved anomalies at ~300 m scale (50x finer than satellite map), and reduced long-term drift ~70x in a 56 h stationary test.
conclusion: This provides the first GNSS-independent gravity-map-matching navigation demonstration with a quantum gravimeter, pointing toward compact quantum sensing for GNSS-denied navigation and survey.

title: Threshold Spectral Transition For A Fermion-boson Pair On The One-dimensional Lattice
authors: Shakhobiddin I. Khamidov Sobir S. Ulashov
abstract: ArXiv:2608.25582v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a two-particle lattice Schr\"odinger operator describing a fermion-boson pair on the one-dimensional lattice [MATH] with zero-range on-site interaction of strength [MATH] and mass ratio [MATH]. Using relative coordinates and fiber decomposition with respect to the total quasi-momentum [MATH], we obtain a real symmetric fiber Hamiltonian [MATH] in [MATH] with essential spectrum $[MATH][MATH]a_\gamma(k)>0[MATH]\mu\ne0[MATH][MATH][MATH]\mu<0[MATH]\mu>0[MATH](\gamma,k)=(1,\pi)[MATH]{4}[MATH]E_1(\pi,\mu)=4+\mu[MATH]\mu=0[MATH]a_\gamma(k)>0[MATH]\mu\to0^\pm[MATH][MATH][MATH]E_\gamma(k,\mu)=\mu+2(1+\gamma)+O(|\mu|^{-1})[MATH]\mu\to0^\pm[MATH](\gamma,k)\to(1,\pi)[MATH]|\mu|[MATH]a_\gamma(k)$, revealing the nonuniformity of the weak-coupling threshold asymptotics.
tldr: The paper studies the spectral properties of a fermion-boson pair on a one-dimensional lattice, focusing on a threshold transition in the weak-coupling limit.
motivation: To understand the spectrum of a two-particle lattice Schrödinger operator with on-site interaction, particularly the behavior near the threshold and its dependence on mass ratio and interaction strength.
method: Using relative coordinates, fiber decomposition, and analysis of the fiber Hamiltonian, the authors derive asymptotic expansions of eigenvalues as the coupling parameter tends to zero.
result: They identify a threshold spectral transition at specific parameter regimes and show nonuniformity of weak-coupling asymptotics near the transition point.
conclusion: The findings reveal intricate spectral behavior in this lattice model, contributing to mathematical physics but not directly related to quantum information processing.

title: Characterizing Full Nonequilibrium Dynamics Of Simple Exclusion Processes
authors: Zhimao Liu, Jing Liu, Pan Zhang, Ying Tang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.25606v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The simple exclusion process (SEP) is a paradigmatic model for nonequilibrium transport, yet the rich dynamics of its time-dependent joint distribution over an exponentially large configuration space remain notoriously intractable. Here, we leverage variational autoregressive networks to systematically characterize the nonequilibrium dynamics of symmetric (SSEP), asymmetric (ASEP), and totally asymmetric (TASEP) cases from one to three dimensions. We first validate the approach by reproducing the previous finite-time results for the 1D SSEP and long-time tensor-network results for the 2D SSEP, and then provide richer finite-time dynamics of the SSEP, ASEP, and TASEP in 1D and 2D, and a new finite-time analysis in 3D. Specifically, in 1D, we reveal that finite-time dynamical-activity maps directly correspond to the classical three-phase TASEP steady-state organization, and, in the long-time limit, boundary and bulk effects separately govern the dynamical susceptibility during the crossover from diffusive to ballistic transport. In 2D, we establish a mean-field directional-density criterion, supported by our neural-network calculations, and show that long-time boundary and bulk effects mirror their 1D counterparts. In 3D, we uncover new finite-time scaling relations for the active-inactive phase transition of the SSEP, and reveal a broadly consistent scaling exponent of the phase-transition point versus system size, implying that the phase-transition point is asymptotically controlled by the characteristic length scale ([MATH]) regardless of dimension. This work thus establishes a unified framework for characterizing the nonequilibrium dynamics of representative transport systems.
tldr: This paper uses variational autoregressive networks to characterize the full nonequilibrium dynamics of simple exclusion processes (SSEP, ASEP, TASEP) in 1D, 2D, and 3D, revealing dynamics of phase transitions and transport.
motivation: Simple exclusion processes are paradigmatic for nonequilibrium transport, but their time-dependent joint distributions are intractable; the authors aim to systematically characterize their dynamics using neural networks.
method: They employ variational autoregressive networks to approximate the time-dependent joint distributions, validate against known results, and then apply to various dimensions and asymmetry cases.
result: They reproduce known results, then provide new finite-time dynamics in 1D and 2D, and a novel 3D analysis, revealing connections between dynamical activity and phase organization and finding scaling relations for phase transitions.
conclusion: The work establishes a unified framework for characterizing nonequilibrium dynamics of transport systems using neural networks, applicable across dimensions.

title: A Symmetry-Preserving Tensor $\star_{\mathbf{M}}$-SVD
authors: Misha E. Kilmer Victor Arsenescu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.24985v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multiway data such as image collections and video is ubiquitous, but the usual approach of flattening them into matrices discards the cross-mode structure that often carries the signal. The t-product and its generalization, the [MATH]-product, give a matrix-mimetic tensor algebra with a tensor SVD whose truncation is optimal in the Frobenius norm, just as in the matrix case. Much real data also has internal reflective symmetry: frontal faces, manufactured parts, and leaves are all bilaterally symmetric. We define a symmetry-preserving [MATH]-SVD that extends the matrix symmetry-preserving SVD of Shah and Sorensen to the [MATH]-algebra. When a tensor's transform-domain frontal slices are reflectively symmetric, the left basis of its [MATH]-SVD is symmetric too, so only its top half must be stored. Bilaterally symmetric images, turned on their side and stored as lateral slices, give such a tensor. This construction keeps the symmetric part of each image and stores only half the basis. We then recognize new images by projecting them onto this basis and matching to the nearest training image in coefficient space. Across ten datasets of faces, leaves, butterfly wings, and other objects, the symmetric basis matches the recognition rate of ordinary tensor SVD at 2-11x less basis storage, with the exception of MUCT. On faces under varying illumination it exceeds the best rate the ordinary tensor SVD attains at any storage level.
tldr: The paper presents a symmetry-preserving tensor SVD for multiway data with reflective symmetry, achieving efficient storage and competitive image recognition performance.
motivation: Multiway data like image collections is common, but flattening discards cross-mode structure. The authors aim to exploit internal reflective symmetry to reduce storage while preserving recognition accuracy.
method: They define a symmetry-preserving M-product SVD that extends matrix symmetry-preserving SVD to the tensor algebra, storing only half the basis for reflectively symmetric tensors, and use projection onto this symmetric basis for image recognition.
result: Across ten datasets (faces, leaves, butterfly wings), the symmetric basis achieves the same recognition rate as ordinary tensor SVD with 2-11x less basis storage, and on faces under varying illumination it exceeds the best ordinary SVD rate.
conclusion: The symmetry-preserving tensor SVD effectively reduces storage for symmetric multiway data without sacrificing recognition performance, offering a practical advantage in image recognition tasks.

title: A Schr\"odinger Characterization Of The Oscillator Semigroup
authors: Gianluca Giacchi
abstract: ArXiv:2608.25082v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The oscillator (or metaplectic) semigroup is classically defined as the two-fold cover of the semigroup of positive complex symplectic matrices. Although geometrically precise, this definition does not provide an intrinsic operator-theoretic characterization of the bounded operators corresponding to positive symplectic matrices. This is in contrast with the real metaplectic group, whose relation with the symplectic group can be expressed directly in terms of the Schr\"odinger representation of the Heisenberg group through its intertwining property. In the complex setting, such a relation appears in the existing literature mainly in infinitesimal form or on suitable classes of Gaussian functions. In this work we prove that the (complexified) Schr\"odinger intertwining relation holds for every function in [MATH]. The main point is the converse statement: if an arbitrary complex symplectic matrix [MATH] admits a nonzero bounded operator on [MATH] satisfying this intertwining relation, then [MATH] is necessarily positive and the operator coincides, up to a nonzero scalar, with the corresponding element of the oscillator semigroup. Consequently, positive complex symplectic matrices are exactly those admitting a nonzero bounded Schr\"odinger intertwiner, and the associated intertwining space is one-dimensional. This provides a Schr\"odinger-representation characterization of the oscillator semigroup, parallel to the classical one for the real metaplectic group.
tldr: The paper provides a Schrödinger-representation characterization of the oscillator semigroup by proving that positive complex symplectic matrices are exactly those admitting a nonzero bounded intertwining operator.
motivation: The classical definition of the oscillator semigroup lacks an intrinsic operator-theoretic characterization, unlike the real metaplectic group.
method: The author proves the complexified Schrödinger intertwining relation for all functions in a suitable space, and conversely shows that any complex symplectic matrix admitting a nonzero bounded intertwiner must be positive, confirming the operator coincides with the semigroup element.
result: Positive complex symplectic matrices are precisely those admitting a nonzero bounded Schrödinger intertwiner, and the intertwining space is one-dimensional.
conclusion: This yields a Schrödinger-representation characterization of the oscillator semigroup, parallel to the classical real case.

title: Approximating Energy-Regulation Feasible Region Of Virtual Power Plants: A Data-driven Inverse Optimization Approach
authors: Ruike Lyu, Hongye Guo, Qixin Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2608.25248v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: System operators will probably allow virtual power plants (VPPs) to submit their feasible region (FR) for market clearing and dispatch. A VPP needs to determine its FR to submit as a whole based on the individual operation model of its internal distributed energy resources (DERs), which is an FR aggregation problem. Existing FR aggregation approaches rely on analytical methods, which have issues with generality and adaptability. In this paper, we propose a data-driven approach to approximate the energy-regulation FR of VPPs. It adopts the virtual battery model to approximate the aggregate FR of a VPP and determines the model parameters through inverse optimization based on generated multi-scenario operation data using the original operation model. Numerical tests verified the accuracy of the proposed method. We believe that our work helps to better leverage the flexibility of DERs.
tldr: This paper proposes a data-driven inverse optimization approach to approximate the energy-regulation feasible region of virtual power plants using a virtual battery model.
motivation: Existing analytical methods for feasible region aggregation lack generality and adaptability, motivating a data-driven approach.
method: The method generates multi-scenario operation data from the original operation model and uses inverse optimization to determine parameters of a virtual battery model that approximates the aggregate feasible region.
result: Numerical tests verified the accuracy of the proposed method in approximating the feasible region.
conclusion: The work helps better leverage the flexibility of distributed energy resources by providing a practical approximation method for VPP feasible regions.

title: The Sharp Discrete Hardy Inequality On $\z^3$
authors: Natanael Alpay
abstract: ArXiv:2608.25262v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the sharp constant in the nearest-neighbor Hardy inequality on [MATH] with the Euclidean inverse-square weight. For every finitely supported function [MATH], we prove \[ \sum_{x\in\Z^3}\sum_{j=1}^3 |u(x+e_j)-u(x)|^2 \geq \frac14\sum_{x\in\Z^3\setminus\{0\}} {|x|^2}. \] The coefficient [MATH] is sharp, and equality is not attained by a nonzero finitely supported function. The proof uses an explicit reciprocal edge field and an edgewise completion of squares, together with a concavity argument for the associated vertex weight.
tldr: Determines the sharp constant for the discrete Hardy inequality on Z^3 with Euclidean inverse-square weight.
motivation: To establish the best possible constant in the discrete Hardy inequality on the three-dimensional integer lattice, a fundamental problem in discrete analysis.
method: Uses an explicit reciprocal edge field, an edgewise completion of squares, and a concavity argument for the associated vertex weight.
result: Proves the inequality with sharp constant 1/4 and shows that equality is not attained by a nonzero finitely supported function.
conclusion: Provides a complete solution for the sharp constant in the nearest-neighbor Hardy inequality on Z^3.

title: "Truncated Fourier Filtering" Method For Fast And High-order Evaluation Of Integrals And Convolutions In General Domains
authors: Oscar P. Bruno, Ambuj Pandey, Krishna Y. Poojara
abstract: ArXiv:2608.25264v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper introduces and analyzes a novel algorithm---Truncated Fourier Filtering (TFF)---for the fast, high-order accurate evaluation of standard integrals and convolutions involving piecewise-smooth (possibly discontinuous) integrands over general [MATH]-dimensional domains ([MATH]) employing an [MATH]-dimensional Cartesian grid. For an [MATH]-point discretization, the method runs at a computational cost of [MATH] operations for standard integrals and [MATH] operations for convolutions, following, in either case, a one-time [MATH] precomputation step (not required in dimension [MATH]). The core idea underlying TFF is to approximate the characteristic function of the integration domain by a truncated Fourier expansion of it over a suitably extended periodic domain, and to evaluate the resulting integrals via trapezoidal quadrature on a Cartesian grid with an appropriately chosen discretization size. Despite its conceptual simplicity, TFF attains high-order accuracy even for complex, possibly non-smooth or even non-Lipschitz geometries. A complete theoretical analysis is provided that establishes the superalgebraic convergence (i.e., convergence faster than any negative power of [MATH]) of the overall approach.
tldr: Introduces a Truncated Fourier Filtering method for fast, high-order accurate evaluation of integrals and convolutions over general domains using a Cartesian grid.
motivation: Efficiently compute integrals and convolutions of piecewise-smooth functions over possibly non-smooth geometries, which is challenging for traditional methods.
method: Approximates the characteristic function of the integration domain by a truncated Fourier expansion and uses trapezoidal quadrature on a Cartesian grid.
result: Achieves superalgebraic convergence (faster than any negative power of N) with computational cost O(N^d) for integrals and O(N^d log N) for convolutions, plus a one-time O(N^d) precomputation for d>1.
conclusion: The method provides a simple, rigorous, and high-order accurate approach for numeric integration on complex domains, with potential applications in numerical analysis.

title: Schr\"odinger Bridges Over Kinetic Swarming Models
authors: Asmaa Eldesoukey, Md Zulfiqur Haider, Italo Napolitano, Yongxin Chen, Abhishek Halder
abstract: ArXiv:2608.25281v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Paradigmatic interaction models explain how collective behaviors can emerge in complex systems from interactions among the constituent agents. In bio-inspired swarms, however, interactions alone may not suffice to bring the population to a desired aggregate configuration within a prescribed time horizon, as needed in applications ranging from targeted therapy to collective transport and emergency evacuation. In the present work, we consider finite-horizon minimum-energy collective steering for inertial swarms that are subject to stochastic disturbances. We focus on the mean-field representations of these multi-agent systems driven by Cucker--Smale alignment or Morse attraction--repulsion interactions. Our objective is to steer the swarm between prescribed endpoint distributions using a state-feedback control, where the endpoint specifications can be full phase-space distributions (positions and velocities) or position marginals alone. Our formalism is rooted in the theory of Schr\"odinger bridges, which has inspired contemporary developments spanning statistical inference, biological modeling, stochastic control, and generative learning. Within the bridges framework, the uncontrolled interacting stochastic dynamics are viewed as a prior model, and the optimal control as the minimum-energy corrective drift needed to realize the prescribed distributions. We derive nonlinear, coupled necessary optimality systems with a time-symmetric structure reminiscent of classical Schr\"odinger bridges, and propose nested fixed-point schemes to numerically solve them. Numerical examples show that the obtained optimal control (corrective drift) can dynamically exploit or counteract the interaction forces, depending on whether the latter are favorable or adversarial to the steering task.
tldr: This paper applies Schrödinger bridge theory to steer inertial swarms under stochastic disturbances using optimal control, targeting collective behaviors in multi-agent systems.
motivation: To achieve desired aggregate configurations in bio-inspired swarms within a fixed time horizon, which is essential for applications like targeted therapy and emergency evacuation, but interactions alone may not suffice.
method: The uncontrolled interacting stochastic dynamics serve as a prior, and the optimal control is derived as a minimum-energy corrective drift within the Schrödinger bridge framework. Nested fixed-point schemes solve the coupled nonlinear optimality systems.
result: Numerical examples show that the optimal control can dynamically exploit or counteract interaction forces depending on whether they are favorable or adversarial to the steering task.
conclusion: The Schrödinger bridge formalism offers a systematic and effective approach for mean-field steering of inertial swarms, with potential extensions to other collective dynamics.

title: Accelerated Gradient Flow With Endogenous Gradient-Memory Anchor: Selection And Restoring Damping
authors: Chinedu Izuchukwu, Ernest Obini, Jen-Chih Yao, Shengda Zeng
abstract: ArXiv:2608.25312v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce an accelerated gradient flow with an endogenous gradient-memory anchor and a nonlinear restoring--damping feedback. The anchor evolves from a weighted history of the gradients, while the nonlinear feedback is modulated by the squared coordinatewise displacement from the anchor. The resulting dynamics uses only first-order information from the objective function and does not involve explicit Hessian information. Under suitable assumptions, we establish global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions. A Lyapunov analysis yields the accelerated objective-value estimate [MATH], with the nonlinear restoring--damping term contributing additional dissipation. Under similar assumptions, the primal trajectory converges strongly to a minimizer. When, in addition, the solution set [MATH] is affine, the limit is identified explicitly as the Euclidean projection [MATH] of the initial anchor [MATH] onto [MATH]. In particular, for rank-deficient least-squares problems, the dynamics selects the least-squares solution closest to [MATH]. We also establish a finite weighted dissipation estimate for the phase variable. Moreover, in coordinates where the nonlinear feedback is active, if the trajectory remains separated from the anchor over an interval, then the corresponding homogeneous phase dynamics acquires an additional polynomial decay factor. Numerical experiments illustrate the minimizer-selection, accelerated objective-value decay, and restoring--damping mechanisms.
tldr: This paper introduces an accelerated gradient flow with an endogenous gradient-memory anchor and nonlinear restoring-damping feedback, proving convergence and minimizer selection properties.
motivation: To develop a first-order optimization dynamics that accelerates convergence and selects specific minimizers without requiring Hessian information.
method: The authors propose a gradient flow with a weighted gradient-memory anchor and a nonlinear damping term based on displacement from the anchor, then perform Lyapunov analysis to establish convergence rates and strong convergence.
result: They establish global existence, uniqueness, accelerated objective-value decay, and strong convergence to a minimizer, with explicit projection in the affine case and polynomial decay under separation from the anchor.
conclusion: The dynamics offers a novel first-order method with enhanced dissipation and minimizer selection, though it is in the field of optimization, not quantum information or related fields.

title: Towards Faithful And Efficient Semantic Communication: An Ontological Approach
authors: Yixiao Feng, Yueting Wang, Yining Wang, Han Han, Bo Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.25422v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, an ontology-driven semantic communication (ODSC) framework is proposed for multi-view visual question answering (VQA) tasks. In the considered framework, multiple transmitters observe a scene, extract the semantic information (SI) with vision-language models (VLMs), and transmit the scene graphs to a receiver. Due to the completeness, heterogeneity, and uninterpretability of the VLMs, the extracted scene graphs are redundant, ambiguous, and inconsistent. To solve these problems, the transmitters and the receiver share an ontology-based knowledge base that predefines synonyms, inference rules, and consistency constraints. For each transmitter, the proposed ODSC framework removes the partial scene graph that can be inferred based on the inference rules. For the receiver, the proposed framework aligns the SI of different views based on the synonyms and detects the inconsistency among the views based on the constraints. A metric of multi-view VQA accuracy (MVA) is defined to evaluate the proposed framework. Simulation results show that, compared with transmitting the complete scene graphs, the proposed framework reduces the data size of the SI by up to 87.1% while improving the answering accuracy by 4.5%. Moreover, the proposed framework yields up to a 16.0% improvement in terms of the MVA compared with the SI filtering approaches.
tldr: An ontology-driven semantic communication framework for multi-view VQA that reduces data size and improves accuracy.
motivation: The extracted scene graphs from VLMs are redundant, ambiguous, and inconsistent, leading to inefficiency and errors.
method: The framework shares an ontology-based knowledge base with synonyms, inference rules, and consistency constraints to remove redundant partial scene graphs, align semantic information, and detect inconsistencies.
result: Simulation shows up to 87.1% reduction in data size and 4.5% improvement in answering accuracy, with up to 16.0% improvement in multi-view VQA accuracy over filtering approaches.
conclusion: The ontology-based approach enhances efficiency and faithfulness in semantic communication for multi-view tasks.

title: Joint Beamforming Design And Port Selection In Fluid Antenna-Assisted Multi-Cell Networks: A Personalized Federated Learning Approach
authors: Liwen Gao, Li Zheng, Xing Hao, Ziru Chen, Lin X. Cai
abstract: ArXiv:2608.25514v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates joint beamforming and port selection in multi-cell fluid antenna-assisted (FAS) networks. In such networks, active beamforming and discrete FA port selection are coupled through intra-cell and inter-cell interference and are jointly optimized to maximize the weighted sum-rate (WSR). We develop a federated representation learning (FedRep) framework with a position-aware dual-branch deep neural network (PA-DNN). The PA-DNN uses channel state information and port positional encoding as inputs, and jointly outputs beamforming vectors and port selections through two task-specific branches. To support decentralized training across heterogeneous cells, the FedRep framework shares global beamforming-related parameters among base stations while keeping port-selection parameters local for cell-specific adaptation. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme achieves a higher weighted sum-rate than conventional FL and port-selection benchmark schemes.
tldr: This paper proposes a personalized federated learning approach for joint beamforming and port selection in fluid antenna-assisted multi-cell networks to maximize weighted sum-rate.
motivation: In fluid antenna systems, the joint optimization of beamforming and port selection is coupled through interference, and decentralized training across heterogeneous cells is needed.
method: They develop a federated representation learning (FedRep) framework with a position-aware dual-branch deep neural network (PA-DNN) that outputs beamforming vectors and port selections, sharing global beamforming parameters while keeping port-selection parameters local.
result: Simulations show higher weighted sum-rate than conventional FL and port-selection benchmarks.
conclusion: The scheme effectively leverages personalized federated learning for joint optimization in multi-cell fluid antenna networks.

title: Adaptive Hybrid Subspace Levenberg Marquardt Algorithm With Adequacy Monitor For Large Scale Least Squares Problems
authors: Timothy J. Lewis M. Duc Hoang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.25524v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Levenberg-Marquardt (LM) algorithm is the most widely used method for solving nonlinear least-squares problems, as it combines the robustness of steepest descent with the fast local convergence of the Gauss-Newton method. However, its computational cost can become prohibitive for large-scale problems because each iteration requires solving a large damped linear system, and conventional step acceptance strategies may require repeated solves as the damping parameter is adjusted. Despite this computational challenge, many large-scale least-squares problems exhibit effective low-dimensional structure, with only a small number of parameter-space directions strongly informed by the data. We propose an adaptive hybrid subspace Levenberg-Marquardt (HSLM) algorithm that constructs a low-dimensional subspace from complementary sources of gradient, memory, Krylov-subspace, and randomized curvature information and computes a spectrally damped LM step within this subspace. A distinguishing feature of the method is a deterministic adequacy monitor that quantifies how much descent information is captured by the reduced space and adaptively enriches the subspace when necessary. Step acceptance is decoupled from damping adjustment: Armijo backtracking determines the accepted step length, while the ratio of actual to predicted reduction is used solely to update the damping parameter, thereby avoiding repeated damped-system solves during step acceptance. For the HSLM algorithm, we establish global convergence to stationarity and prove local linear and superlinear convergence. Numerical experiments on neural-network training problems show that HSLM achieves convergence behavior comparable to classical and Krylov subspace LM (KSLM) while substantially reducing per-iteration computational cost, with increasing advantages observed as the parameter dimension grows.
tldr: An adaptive hybrid subspace Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm for large-scale least squares problems that uses low-dimensional subspaces and an adequacy monitor to reduce computational cost.
motivation: Standard LM is computationally expensive for large-scale problems due to repeated damped system solves, but many problems have low-dimensional structure that can be exploited.
method: Constructs a low-dimensional subspace from gradient, memory, Krylov, and randomized curvature information; uses an adequacy monitor to adaptively enrich the subspace, and decouples step acceptance from damping adjustment.
result: Proves global convergence and local superlinear convergence; numerical experiments on neural network training show reduced per-iteration cost while maintaining convergence behavior.
conclusion: The algorithm efficiently solves large-scale least squares problems with lower computational cost, making it suitable for high-dimensional optimization.

title: Constrained Maximum Entropy Contiguous Aggregations
authors: Ugo Vaccaro Roberto Bruno
abstract: ArXiv:2608.25533v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a probability distribution [MATH] and an integer [MATH], a contiguous aggregation of [MATH] is a probability distribution [MATH] such that each [MATH] is a sum of consecutive elements of [MATH]. Given [MATH] and a positive number [MATH], we consider the problem of computing a maximum entropy contiguous aggregation [MATH] of [MATH], under the constraint that its Shannon entropy [MATH] is at most [MATH]. We devise a dynamic programming algorithm that solves the problem exactly, and two time-efficient greedy algorithms that provide close-to-optimal solutions. We discuss a few scenarios where our problem arises.
tldr: This paper presents algorithms to find a contiguous aggregation of a probability distribution that maximizes entropy subject to an entropy upper bound.
motivation: The problem arises in scenarios where probability distributions need to be summarized or compressed while preserving information content within a specified entropy limit.
method: The authors devise an exact dynamic programming algorithm and two time-efficient greedy algorithms for near-optimal solutions.
result: The dynamic programming algorithm solves the problem exactly, and the greedy algorithms provide close-to-optimal solutions in less time.
conclusion: The paper offers computational methods for constrained maximum entropy aggregation, with potential applications in data compression and summarization.

title: Exactly Diagonal Gram Matrices In Jacobi Weighted Histopolation
authors: Allal Guessab, Federico Nudo, Stefano Serra-Capizzano
abstract: ArXiv:2608.25714v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the current work, we study univariate polynomial weighted histopolation on [MATH], where the data are weighted integrals over a family of intervals. After choosing a polynomial basis, the weighted moment conditions lead to a histopolation matrix whose structure depends on the weight and on the geometry of the cells. We investigate its nonsingularity, which guarantees unisolvence, together with exact diagonality of its Gram matrix, which allows its singular values and spectral condition number to be determined explicitly. For families of intervals whose endpoints belong to a fixed grid, we characterize unisolvence in terms of the connectedness of the associated endpoint graph. In the unisolvent case, this graph is a tree, and the unique paths joining consecutive grid points provide an explicit expression for the inverse matrix. This identity gives explicit formulas for the singular values of both matrices, and shows that their condition numbers in the two-norm coincide and grow linearly with the matrix size. Moreover, it yields the limiting singular value distributions of the two matrix sequences. We also establish a general diagonalization criterion based on discrete weighted orthogonality. The criterion recovers the first kind Chebyshev construction and leads to a diagonal configuration for the constant weight based on discrete sine orthogonality. For interval families with a connected endpoint graph, the corresponding moment vectors define an inner product on the polynomial space and lead to a monic basis with a diagonal weighted Gram matrix. Finally, we derive reduction formulas for cell moments associated with generalized Jacobi weights and introduce an alternative basis for shifted Jacobi weights. Applied to the Chebyshev weight of the fourth kind, this basis, together with a correction of one nonconstant element, yields an exactly diagonal Gram matrix.
tldr: This paper studies univariate polynomial weighted histopolation, focusing on the structure of histopolation matrices and their Gram matrices, achieving exact diagonality and explicit singular values and condition numbers.
motivation: The authors aim to understand the nonsingularity and spectral properties of histopolation matrices arising from weighted integrals over intervals, which is important for approximation and interpolation.
method: They analyze the structure of the histopolation matrix, characterize unisolvence via graph connectedness, derive explicit inverse matrix expressions using paths in trees, and establish diagonalization criteria based on discrete weighted orthogonality.
result: They provide explicit formulas for singular values and condition numbers, show linear growth of condition numbers, establish limiting singular value distributions, and present a diagonalization criterion that recovers Chebyshev constructions.
conclusion: The paper advances the theoretical understanding of weighted histopolation, offering diagonal configurations for certain weights and explicit spectral information.

title: Quantitative Tiling Stability From Quadratic Discrepancy In Hamming Spaces
authors: Valery (binyamin), Grishin (yohananov), Aryeh Lev Zabokritskiy
abstract: ArXiv:2608.25716v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quadratic ball discrepancy defines an energy on codes in finite Hamming spaces. At perfect-code parameters, its exact minimizers are the perfect codes. We fix the alphabet size, length, and code cardinality and compare all codes with these parameters. We prove tiling-defect stability: excess discrepancy above the perfect-code benchmark controls the squared deviation of the distinguished ball-covering multiplicity from one. For one-error parameters satisfying sphere-packing and Lloyd integrality, the lower coefficient is [MATH]. The uniform floor one is sharp, while the certified parameter-dependent coefficient can be much larger. An explicit parameter-dependent upper estimate is also available, and the two certified coefficients can be far apart. For any two-error parameter pair with [MATH] satisfying sphere-packing divisibility and having two distinct integral Lloyd roots in the Hamming weight range, we obtain an explicit positive coefficient without assuming that a perfect code exists. For alphabets of size at least four, this conditional coefficient has a closed form and fixed-alphabet asymptotics. Direct certificates for the repetition and Golay families, combined with perfect-code classification, give tiling-defect stability for every nontrivial perfect code. Here stability concerns the ball-covering multiplicity profile, not symmetric-difference proximity to a particular perfect code. The defect is also a normalized chi-square smoothing error under uniform ball noise, so excess discrepancy controls holes, overlaps, defective ambient points, total variation, and R\'enyi divergence from uniformity of the ball-noise output. Competing codes need not be linear or satisfy a distance or error-correction constraint.
tldr: This paper proves quantitative tiling-stability results for perfect codes in Hamming spaces by showing that excess quadratic ball discrepancy controls the squared deviation of ball-covering multiplicity from one.
motivation: To understand how close general codes are to perfect codes in terms of covering properties, and to provide explicit bounds on defect parameters without assuming code linearity or error-correction constraints.
method: Introduces a quadratic ball discrepancy energy on codes, uses sphere-packing and Lloyd integrality conditions to prove that excess discrepancy above the perfect-code benchmark bounds the squared deviation of covering multiplicity from one, and derives parameter-dependent lower and upper coefficients.
result: Obtains explicit positive stability coefficients for one-error and two-error parameter sets, including closed forms for alphabets of size at least four, and establishes stability for repetition and Golay code families using perfect-code classification.
conclusion: The stability result provides a robust measure of proximity to perfect codes via ball-covering multiplicity profiles and Rényi divergence, contributing to coding theory but not directly relevant to quantum information or other listed research directions.

title: Learning Of Deep Neural Network Regression Estimates Using Gradient Descent With Pruning
authors: Michael Kohler, Vincent Molinero R\"omer, Adam Krzy\.zak
abstract: ArXiv:2608.25743v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Estimation of a regression function from independent and identically distributed data is considered. The [MATH] error with integration with respect to the design variable is used as the error criterion. An initially randomly pruned fully connected deep neural network with logistic squasher as activation function is fitted to the data via gradient descent, using a data-dependent choice of non-constant stepsizes during gradient descent. It is shown that this network achieves (up to a logarithmic factor) the optimal minimax rate of convergence in case that the regression function is [MATH]--smooth. Here the estimate is able to circumvent the curse of dimensionality provided the predictors are concentrated in the neighborhood of a low dimensional manifold. The finite sample size performance of the estimate is illustrated by applying it to the simulated data.
tldr: This paper proposes a randomly pruned deep neural network with gradient descent that achieves the optimal minimax rate for regression estimation, avoiding the curse of dimensionality under a low-dimensional manifold assumption.
motivation: The goal is to develop a regression estimator that achieves optimal convergence rates in high-dimensional settings while remaining computationally feasible.
method: A fully connected deep neural network with logistic activation is randomly pruned, then fitted via gradient descent using data-dependent step sizes.
result: The estimate achieves (up to a logarithmic factor) the optimal minimax rate for p-smooth regression functions, and can circumvent the curse of dimensionality when predictors lie near a low-dimensional manifold.
conclusion: The proposed method offers a theoretically sound approach to regression with strong convergence guarantees in high-dimensional settings, validated on simulated data.

title: Error Analysis Of The Inverse Conductivity Problem With Scattered Measurements
authors: Bangti Jin, Qimeng Quan, Wenlong Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.25749v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we investigate the inverse problem of recovering the conductivity coefficient in an elliptic equation from noisy measurements collected at finitely many deterministic scattered points in the domain [MATH], and corrupted by random noise. Inspired by the regularity analysis, we propose a numerical scheme based on the regularized least-squares formulation with a [MATH] penalty, and discretize the regularized problem using the Galerkin finite element method with continuous piecewise linear elements. Under suitable assumptions on the problem data, we provide an error analysis of the regularized solution and its Galerkin approximation. We establish [MATH] error bounds in a high-probability sense, which depend explicitly on the regularization parameter [MATH], the number [MATH] of data points and the mesh size [MATH]. We also present numerical experiments to illustrate the theoretical findings.
tldr: This paper provides an error analysis for a regularized least-squares finite element method to recover the conductivity coefficient in an elliptic equation from noisy scattered measurements.
motivation: The inverse conductivity problem is important in applications, but rigorous error bounds for numerical solutions with random noise are lacking.
method: They propose a regularized least-squares formulation with a penalty term, discretized via Galerkin FEM with piecewise linear elements, and derive high-probability error bounds.
result: Explicit error bounds are established that depend on the regularization parameter, number of data points, and mesh size, and numerical experiments validate the theory.
conclusion: The method is theoretically justified and effective, providing a foundation for practical solutions to the inverse conductivity problem with noisy data.

title: Pooling Mobility Obscures Epidemic Invasion Routes
authors: Wei Yang Tiandong Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.25766v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Epidemic models often pool air travel, commuting, and other mobility layers into a single weighted network. Pooling keeps the total imported infections into a region but discards the transport mode and route that delivered them, the information a mode-specific intervention needs. We make this precise for directed multilayer flows with heavy-tailed variation. Pooling acts as an asymmetric filter. The magnitude of an extreme importation, its radial tail index, is an exact invariant of sampling and nonnegative aggregation, whereas its composition across layers and routes, the angular part, is reweighted by layer-specific sampling and can be irrecoverably merged. We give a necessary and sufficient condition for recovering route composition, attach a surveillance decision cost to the loss, and show that the first established route need not be the busiest. A controlled metapopulation study calibrates the cost, and two contrasting reconstructions show where it bites. In US pandemic influenza, air adds fitted information beyond commuting, and a layer-resolved ranking targets more air-import burden than a pooled one. In the early Italian COVID-19 wave, commuting improves onset reconstruction while air attribution stays unresolved. Pooling can therefore support total-importation surveillance but cannot in general identify the mode or route behind an importation.
tldr: Pooling mobility data into a single network obscures specific epidemic invasion routes, and the information loss is quantified.
motivation: To understand how aggregating mobility layers hides the transport modes and routes that deliver infections, which is essential for targeted interventions.
method: The paper analyzes directed multilayer flows with heavy-tailed variation, formalizing pooling as an asymmetric filter. It studies the radial tail index as an invariant and the angular composition under reweighting, and applies the framework to US influenza and Italian COVID-19 data.
result: Pooling preserves the total importation magnitude but irrecoverably merges route composition. A necessary and sufficient condition for recovery is given, and case studies show that air travel adds information beyond commuting and that pooled rankings can misallocate importation burden.
conclusion: Pooling supports total-importation surveillance but cannot identify the specific mode or route behind an importation, limiting its use for mode-specific interventions.

title: Retrieved But Not Reliable: A Survey On Attacks, And Defenses In Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Minh Tran, Cuong Dang, Tuc Nguyen, Khanh-Tung Tran, Minh Huynh Nguyen, Trinh Chau, Kien Le, Do Xuan Long, Jiahao Zhang, Hoang D. Nguyen, Thanh Le, Suhang Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.24977v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) enhances large language models by grounding outputs in external knowledge, improving factuality and reducing hallucinations. At the same time, the retrieval-augmented pipeline introduces new robustness and security risks, including corpus poisoning, backdoor attacks, privacy leakage, and fairness violations. Despite rapid progress in this area, existing surveys remain limited in their treatment of attacker objectives, threat models, and stage-specific defenses across the full RAG pipeline. This survey presents a unified and pipeline-aware overview of RAG robustness. We formalize threat models over the corpus, retriever, and generator, and organize attacks into three main objectives: accuracy, privacy, and fairness. We further review defenses from a pipeline-aware perspective, covering the retrieval, rerank, generation, and traceback stages. In addition, we summarize robustness benchmarks and explainability methods for more deeply evaluating and explaining RAG robustness.
tldr: This paper surveys attacks and defenses in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, categorizing threats by attacker objectives and pipeline stage.
motivation: RAG enhances LLMs with external knowledge but introduces new security risks like corpus poisoning and privacy leakage; existing surveys lack a pipeline-aware, objective-based overview.
method: The authors formalize threat models for corpus, retriever, and generator, organize attacks by accuracy, privacy, and fairness objectives, and review stage-specific defenses across retrieval, rerank, generation, and traceback.
result: A unified and pipeline-aware taxonomy of RAG attacks and defenses, including robustness benchmarks and explainability methods.
conclusion: The survey provides a comprehensive framework for understanding and evaluating RAG robustness, highlighting the need for stage-specific and objective-aware security measures.

title: Static Detection Of Post-Quantum Cryptographic Algorithms In Stripped Binaries For Digital Forensic Examination And Migration Assurance
authors: Muhammad Shaheer Bin Junaid
abstract: ArXiv:2608.25122v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Currently, there is no method to verify from compiled binary code whether a quantum-vulnerable algorithm has been replaced by an approved post-quantum algorithm. Cryptographic discovery tools identify algorithms by symbols, library dependencies, and runtime behaviour; however, all these signals are destroyed by stripping, statically linking, and optimising a binary. This paper presents Kestrel, a static analysis method for identifying the standardised lattice-based schemes ML-KEM and ML-DSA in stripped binary code. Kestrel identifies ML-KEM and ML-DSA by detecting the number-theoretic transform constant tables that form the read-only data upon which the arithmetic depends.
